contract.proof: The host delegates semantics then projects terminal effects/layout without scanning another component owner.
contract.adversarialWitness: Maximum canonical domain with every emitted command projected to the screen owner.

fullScan.rationale: Current canonical transitions may validate a full domain; terminal may not duplicate that semantic scan.

variables.name: k
variables.meaning: closed layers in the committed transition
variables.ceiling: accepted Core layer count, at most 100000

variables.name: n
variables.meaning: live registered callbacks after the transition and reentrant work

assumptions: Core transition computation and arbitrary application callback work have separate bounds.
Map lookup/deletion is expected constant time.
ceilings: Every old registry entry is detached before the first callback; only live replacement registrations remain afterward.
deterministicWork: Repeated same-ID replacement churn confirms zero old entries at first callback, two replacement entries after the cascade, and zero after actual replacement dismissal.
contract.resourceRationale: One transient callback vector replaces the former ID vector. It belongs only to the current synchronous cascade; the existing map owns current registrations. Errors do not prevent draining.
contract.proof: The executor maps committed commands to detached old callbacks in one pass, then drains that snapshot preserving the first thrown value. Later callbacks never re-read the mutable registry.
contract.adversarialWitness: Leaf callbacks replace both ancestor and initiating IDs; normal and throwing callbacks, undefined errors, reentrant close attempts and 64 churn cycles.

fullScan.rationale: Only the k removed registrations are visited, never unrelated live registrations.

variables.name: q
variables.meaning: intrinsic measurement requests in one render, including cache hits
variables.ceiling: requests made by layout and uncached subtree traversal

variables.name: p
variables.meaning: distinct requested node identity and maximum width/height states

variables.name: e
variables.meaning: child edges examined across distinct measurement states
variables.ceiling: sum of child counts for uncached container states

variables.name: t
variables.meaning: text code units scanned across distinct measurement states
variables.ceiling: sum of text lengths for uncached text states

variables.name: d
variables.ceiling: finite acyclic input depth; explicit heap-owned frames

assumptions: Acyclic node descriptors and their constraints remain stable during one synchronous render; different render calls may observe changed descriptors.
WeakMap and numeric Map operations have expected constant cost. Unicode width/wrap walks are proportional to text input under the existing grapheme contract.

This contract covers intrinsic measurement only; cell drawing, frame materialization, serialization and arbitrary accessor work have separate costs. Distinct constraints may require distinct subtree traversals.
ceilings: Each requested node/width/height state produces at most one successful intrinsic measurement per render.
All cached sizes and indexes are generation-local and absent from the returned frame.
deterministicWork: At depth 32/64/128/256 and text length 512/1024/2048/4096 in an 80x1 viewport, each repeated-constraint leaf performs one intrinsic width scan for row and column chains, with or without wrapping.
Fixed-constraint column chains read child lists at most six times per container across measurement and rendering, rather than repeatedly visiting ancestor suffixes.
Shared nodes under different width/height pairs match independently duplicated inputs; repeated, failed and reentrant renders keep their measurement owners independent.
contract.resourceRationale: The private mutable frame owns one Size per distinct node/width/height state. Post-order measurement keeps at most d active heap frames with scalar accumulators; children remain input references, except a one-element box child list. Text splitting uses O(t) temporary storage. Cache hits allocate no traversal stack. JavaScript call depth is constant, including width reductions over child and line collections. Neither the frames nor the measurement indexes enter the returned screen.
contract.proof: Both main-axis distribution and cross-axis sizing use the same frame-owned index. Hits return before content reads. Misses descend by pushing one parent frame, then accumulate child sizes and complete parents in a loop. Each successful state is cached once; no recursive measureNode call or variable-length argument spread remains. Fixed-constraint chains keep the independent #15 one-leaf-scan bound.
contract.adversarialWitness: Depth 20000 row/column/box/mixed layouts in a reduced-stack Node process; 131072 child entries and text lines; increasing depth and text at fixed output; repeated references under different constraints; padding, gaps, fill, alignment, Unicode/cursor projection and changed/failed/reentrant render isolation.

fullScan.rationale: Each distinct constraint state requires its intrinsic child/text calculation once. Identical constraints reuse that result within the generation.

assumptions: These bounds cover dense frame materialization; layout traversal and text measurement are separate input-dependent work.
Dimension property access has constant cost; each property is read once into the transaction-local viewport.
ceilings: Rows and columns are each at most 4096, including viewports with a zero axis.
The rows-by-columns product is at most 1048576 cells. Both axis checks precede multiplication, so the product is an exact safe integer.
deterministicWork: Viewport validation performs two dimension reads and constant numeric checks before appearance access, layout traversal, or frame allocation.
Rejected dimensions allocate zero row arrays and cells and read no node or appearance properties.
All accepted allocation lengths, viewport geometry, and returned dimensions use the same validated scalar snapshot.
contract.resourceRationale: The dense mutable frame and immutable output each contain at most 1048576 cells and 4096 row arrays. Empty-width frames still own row arrays. Validation adds no retained state or accepted-path allocation.
contract.proof: renderTerminalScreen snapshots each axis once, rejects malformed values, applies the 4096 axis ceilings, and checks the 1048576 cell budget before allocating. Construction and freezing visit every row and cell, including row-array overhead when columns is zero.
contract.adversarialWitness: Production-bound tests intercept dense allocation before exercising over-limit axes, zero-axis counterexamples, 2^32, safe-integer extremes, and over-budget products of individually valid axes. Inclusive axis and cell limits remain accepted; an appearance getter that changes the caller's dimensions cannot change the validated viewport.

fullScan.rationale: Dense frame output requires its bounded rows and cells; rejected viewport dimensions require no scan.

variables.name: v
variables.meaning: render node occurrences visited, including children subsequently clipped
variables.ceiling: occurrences in the finite layout; a shared node may occur repeatedly

variables.name: a
variables.meaning: child slots in main-size arrays simultaneously held by active container continuations
variables.ceiling: sum of child counts along active render ancestry; at most v

assumptions: Acyclic descriptors remain stable within a synchronous render; property access has constant cost.

This bound covers traversal, rectangle arithmetic and child-size distribution only. Intrinsic measurement, Unicode text walks, border painting and dense frame materialization have separate contracts/costs.
ceilings: Traversal uses constant JavaScript call depth and at most one continuation per active ancestor plus its current child.
Pending siblings share one indexed continuation; the traversal does not enqueue an entire wide child collection.
deterministicWork: A Node process with a 256 KiB stack renders ten 20000-depth row, column, box, mixed and branching layouts with identical cells and first-cursor projection.
Existing #15 counters independently retain one intrinsic leaf scan for repeated constraints and linear child-list reads.
contract.resourceRationale: RenderTask records and main-size arrays belong to one render. A container schedules one child and retains its sibling cursor only when needed; a box paints its border/title before scheduling its sole child. No traversal record is returned or kept between renders.
contract.proof: renderNode drains an explicit LIFO task stack. renderContainer, renderChild and renderBox only schedule tasks and never recursively invoke renderNode. The child continuation resumes after its descendant subtree, preserving depth-first paint, clipping and first-cursor order. Each visited occurrence adds constant bookkeeping apart from its separately accounted child distribution and drawing work.
contract.adversarialWitness: Deep factory-built box chains exercise render descent, nesting them in columns also exercises intrinsic descent. Deep branching chains retain pending siblings while preserving order. Wide child and line collections exercise scalar reductions without variable-argument stack growth.

fullScan.rationale: Rendering visits the requested layout occurrences and skips descent into clipped node rectangles; depth affects owned heap storage rather than call-stack consumption.

assumptions: Raw input is a string array with ordinary array iteration; each element read is O(1).
The bound covers row snapshot ownership; diff comparison and terminal serialization are separate operations.
ceilings: One array of rRow immutable string references per accepted raw frame; retained until replacement or close.
deterministicWork: Each raw row is read exactly once per render, including successive renders of the same caller array.
A closed writer reads zero input rows and emits zero output.
contract.resourceRationale: The writer owns one retained row snapshot. Raw input allocates one shallow array; strings are shared by value. Structured frames reuse their freshly serialized rows. close releases the retained snapshot.
contract.proof: createTerminalScreenWriter copies and freezes raw row references before any output callback. Diffing and retained history use that snapshot, so caller mutation cannot change a published frame. The copy is one pass over rRow rows.
contract.adversarialWitness: Successive renders of the same accessor-backed array at 1k, 10k, and 100k rows count exactly rRow caller reads per render; mutation and truncation between renders still update and clear the affected rows.

fullScan.rationale: A mutable caller-owned row array requires one complete shallow snapshot to isolate the previous frame.

variables.name: n
variables.meaning: toast items searched for the single announcement, zero without an announcement

variables.name: k
variables.ceiling: dismissed items plus at most one announcement

assumptions: Core semantic state storage/computation and arbitrary consumer callback work are separate.
An immutable announcement item is captured during host effect preparation; no previous-state cache is retained.
ceilings: All committed effects are attempted before first failure escapes; rejected operations do not publish.
Nested latest-revision facade publication is not repeated by the outer call.
deterministicWork: Announce, item-change, subscriber and onUpdate failures each preserve the first thrown value and complete the remaining publication phases.
Overflow, timeout and dismiss-all drain their command outputs; same-ID reentrancy retains the original announcement payload.
contract.resourceRationale: Private prepared host effects retain only immutable command payloads for their synchronous dispatch. One revision scalar deduplicates publication. Facade destroy owns subscriber cleanup.
contract.proof: Core's existing controller publication drains host effects and notification. Terminal completes facade publication after a committed throw, records revisions before callback execution, and suppresses stale outer item notification after nested transitions.
contract.adversarialWitness: Multiple command failures, thrown Error/undefined/null, rejected mutations, nested announcements/item callbacks and changed same-ID announcement data.

fullScan.rationale: An announcement resolves its item once; effect and observer walks are proportional to emitted commands and subscribers.

variables.name: lInput
variables.meaning: data listeners on the borrowed TTY at removal
variables.ceiling: application-owned listener count plus one adapter forwarder

resources.listeners: one source data listener while connected; zero owned source listeners after close
resources.timers: no adapter timer; a Node escape timeout may finish on the detached private decoder

assumptions: The borrowed stream follows Node ReadStream and EventEmitter contracts; its data listeners remain externally owned.
Node retains its existing byte decoding semantics and escape timeout on one private Readable per active keyboard.
deterministicWork: One active keyboard and one source data forwarder per TTY; no decoder properties or keypress listeners are added to that TTY.
Each chunk is forwarded synchronously once without a second buffering queue; Node decoding and key normalization retain their input/output bounds.
Close detaches the forwarder, clears private listeners and the application callback, destroys the private readable, and releases ownership even if raw restoration throws.
Repeated close and captured stale data callbacks perform zero decoding or publication.
contract.resourceRationale: The caller stream retains only one adapter data callback until close. External decoders are untouched. Node's pending escape work can retain only the detached private decoder after its listener is removed, not the application callback or input stream.
contract.proof: Removing one source data listener can scan lInput listeners. All other adapter teardown steps touch a fixed private listener set and scalar ownership state. Normal input adds one constant synchronous forwarding dispatch per chunk; no subscriber-domain scan or byte copy is introduced by the bridge.
contract.adversarialWitness: 64 acquire/close cycles cover all raw/flow baselines and verify zero residual decoding. Active, idle, and subsequently installed external decoders keep their listener identities. Fragmented UTF-8/escape input, mid-chunk close, late escape completion, setup failures, and a real Linux ReadStream exercise the public factory.

fullScan.rationale: Only the adapter's own source listener and private decoder resources are removed.
